clauses.reason: Terminated by express supersession or revocation. Section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 names Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) among the orders superseded or revoked. No effective-date wording appears in the section, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03 (a reading, disclosed). The until-further-order contingency of this clause is ended by that order. Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 and Executive Order 10952 are unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed and not claimed as ends.

Terminated by express supersession or revocation: section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 names Executive Order 10222. The transfer of property, records and personnel was a one-time command; the held sources do not date its performance, so no exhaustion date is asserted and the express supersession (dated on signing, 1994-06-03, a reading, disclosed) is the first held end. The executed transfers are accrued effects.

Terminated with the order by section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 (dated on signing, 1994-06-03, a reading, disclosed). The clause only fixes the order's effective date as of March 4, 1951 and has no separate end.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 (16 FR 2247; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, signed March 8, 1951. Inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses: 1, transferring the civil-defense part of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, to remain under the Administrator's jurisdiction until further order of the President; 2, transferring related property, records and personnel; 3, effective as of March 4, 1951. Ending: section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 (59 FR 29525, held government printing) provides that Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) is superseded or revoked; the U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note says the same and gives the date June 3, 1994. Section 904 has no stated effective date, so the end is read as effective on signing, 1994-06-03. Unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed under the unnamed-instruments ruling of 2026-10-21 (they do not name Executive Order 10222 and are not ends): Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 (the editorial note in the held OFR 1989 Codification says it terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration effective 1958-07-01 and consolidated its functions into the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization) and Executive Order 10952 of 1961-07-20 (the same note says civil defense functions were later transferred to the Secretary of Defense). The same 1989 Codification still prints Executive Order 10222 as in force on 1989-01-20, after both events. The plan's own text and Executive Order 10952 do not appear in the held corpus as acting on this order. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments, a statute or order that does not name the target does not end it; the end is the instrument that names it. savings.reason: The transfers of functions, property, records and personnel carried out under the order are accrued effects of the executed transfers. Executive Order 12919 section 903 provides that previously issued orders, regulations and other actions relating to any function affected by that order remain in effect except as inconsistent with it or later amended or revoked, and that nothing in it affects the validity or force of anything done under previous delegations; the 1989 Codification editorial note and the U.S. Code note show the functions continuing in successor agencies. The whole 12919 text is cited as the savings source.
